purpose: Source-backed notable waterfall candidates absent from the named 161-feature Michigan GIS subset; geographical research, not authorized visitor routes.
policy: Each candidate must pass the existing five-axis public visitor promotion gate before entering data/up-waterfalls.json, public waterfall map cards, nearby suggestions or public sitemap. A county-tourism parking note or a generic MDOT highway parking policy does not prove a site-specific lawful turnout and continuous riverbank rights.

records.name: Upper Eagle River Falls (Ten-Foot Falls)
records.near: Phoenix / M-26, between US-41 and Eagle River

geography.identityConclusion: Independent field and two Visit Keweenaw publications identify the upstream waterfall, clearly distinct from curated lower Eagle River Falls (#142). Point-to-point discrepancy remains unresolved; do not assign either coordinate to an arrival or hiking route.

sources.label: Visit Keweenaw 2026–27 official visitor guide, 10-Foot Falls #7
sources.supports: Short unmarked trail off M-26, seasonal runoff; not a maintained signed visitor trail.

sources.label: Keweenaw Waterfalls brochure #7
sources.supports: Small roadside parking area on right about 0.8 mile west of Phoenix M-26; map coordinate 47.4000,-88.2887. Does not certify legal parcel, exact turnout or public riverbank route.

sources.label: Visit Keweenaw two-day waterfall driving tour
sources.supports: Unmarked gravel pull-off and upper-vs-lower distinction, but not site-specific land title or posted turn-out authority.

sources.label: Waterfalls of the Keweenaw, Ten Foot Falls
sources.supports: Independent cascade identity and natural point 47.39735,-88.28439; historical shoulder parking is not current landowner permission.

sources.label: MDOT common FAQ on state highway roadside parking
sources.supports: Roadside parking generally not prohibited, with narrow exceptions and site-specific traffic orders; does not establish exact M-26 pull-off legality or private riverbank access.

sources.label: Michigan State Police traffic control orders and parking restrictions
sources.supports: Specific roadside stopping restrictions depend on traffic orders and safety; a general highway rule does not guarantee parking rights at a site.

sources.label: Keweenaw County Equalization GIS and parcel information
sources.supports: County land-title records are authoritative, but exact shoreline-bank property/visitor easement not verified in this review.

segments.finding: Visit Keweenaw and independent waterfall researcher document this separate upper Eagle River cascade, not Lower Eagle River Bridge Park #142. The two published point locations differ by about 438 metres.
MDOT manages state trunkline M-26; ownership and public-use permission for the precise riverbank from the turnout have not been certified.

Bureau lists a small gravel roadside pull-off, MDOT generally permits roadside parking with exceptions, but no site-specific traffic order, official signed parking area, turnout property survey or live restrictions have been verified.
Bureau labels the short trail unmarked; no authoritative continuous public walking path to an approved bank viewpoint, no current accessible facilities.
Snowplow use, ice, sightlines, deep water and wet volcanic rocks may make this unsuitable even where roadside stopping is permitted.

records.visitorDecision: The waterfall exists and local tourism encourages an unsigned roadside visit. Do not send public visitors to either natural/map coordinate or imply a permitted riverbank footpath until exact parking/right-of-way and land crossing are checked. Direct general visitors to the separately managed, signed Lower Eagle River Bridge Park waterfall instead.
promotionEvidenceNeeded: Resolve the ~438 m bureau-vs-firsthand coordinate discrepancy and identify actual public roadway/viewing sightline without navigational guesses.
Obtain MDOT site-specific roadside/ROW, signage, traffic-order or verified official public parking determination at the actual pull-off; roadside parking permission depends on posted conditions.
Establish exact waterfall bank parcel title or public easement, and continuous walking permission if a bank view requires leaving public ROW.
Provide current seasonal road shoulder/turnout limitations, legal entry and public view safety before an indexable waterfall guide or map stop.
